title: Shell completions for skillz CLI
description:
## Summary

Add shell completion support for the `skillz` CLI so users can tab-complete commands, subcommands, flags, and (where practical) dynamic values.

## Motivation

Discoverability and speed of use for a multi-subcommand CLI. Completions are a standard expectation for developer tools.

## Scope

- Generate and install/document completions for commonly supported shells, at least:
  - bash
  - zsh
  - fish (commonly supported alongside bash/zsh via clap_complete)
- Consider also: elvish, powershell if cheap via the same generator
- Likely approach: clap + `clap_complete` (workspace already uses clap 4 derive)
- Expose a stable UX, e.g. `skillz completions <shell>` (or equivalent) that prints the script to stdout for users to source/install
- Document how to enable completions for each supported shell

## Acceptance criteria (draft)

- [ ] User can generate completion scripts for bash, zsh, and fish
- [ ] Completions cover top-level commands and subcommands/flags
- [ ] README or man/help docs explain how to install/enable completions per shell
- [ ] Completions stay in sync with the clap command tree (generated, not hand-maintained)

## Notes

Keep this small: generation + docs first; dynamic value completion (skill names, library paths) can be a follow-up if not trivial.
close_reason: Met AC: skillz completions for bash/zsh/fish (+ elvish/powershell) via clap_complete; README install notes

title: library import --name to catalog under a different skill name
description:
## Goal
Allow `skillz library import` to record an Upstream Catalog Entry under a name different from the discovered skill directory name (e.g. keep existing `taste-skill` and import GitHub `…/skills/taste-skill` as `taste-skill-main`).

## Acceptance
- CLI: `skillz library import SOURCE --name NEWNAME`
- Only valid when exactly one skill is selected/discovered; otherwise clear error
- Source string still pins the GitHub path/rev; only the catalog `name` changes
- Collision/owned checks use the override name
- Regression test covers rename-past-collision

title: skillz hooks show (dry-run inspection)
description:

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each entry shows target file path and planned contents (dry-run; no writes)
- [ ] Indicates whether each gate is already installed vs would be created/updated
- [ ] Works for git-only, jj (incl. colocated), and reports clearly when neither applies
- [ ] Tests cover show planning for git and jj

1. Clear status line when Remove is changed back to Skip (or any other action)

3. For unlocked skills, suggest a Catalog Entry match and whether the Installation matches exactly (recursive file compare)

### Acceptance

- [ ] Unlocked libcommit/remove paths work without requiring a pre-existing Lock
- [ ] Unlocked rows show suggested Library entry + exact/diff match hint
- [ ] Tests cover match helper and/or status-line reset behavior where practical

title: Fix github tag checkout and https @rev URL parsing for library import
description:
## Problem
`skillz library import github:…@v2.1.0` fails on an existing cache clone:
`fatal: git checkout: --detach does not take a path argument 'v2.1.0'`
because `git fetch --depth 1 origin <tag>` only updates FETCH_HEAD and does not create a local tag ref.

Also HTTPS forms fail:
- `https://github.com/owner/repo@v2.1.0` treats `@v2.1.0` as part of the repo name
- `https://github.com/owner/repo/@v2.1.0` treats `@v2.1.0` as a path
- `…/tree/v2.1.0/…` parses correctly but hits the same checkout bug

## Acceptance
- Cached-clone checkout works for tags, branches, and SHAs
- HTTPS `@rev` and `/@rev` parse to rev (not repo/path)
- Regression tests cover parse + checkout resolution
close_reason: Fixed cached-clone tag checkout via FETCH_HEAD and HTTPS @rev URL parsing

title: Spec: skillz — skills manager CLI/TUI
description:
## Problem Statement

I work across many projects, each with its own set of agent skills. Some skills are Upstream (from other people's GitHub repos), some are Authored by me, some are Forked (started Upstream or Tool-Provided, then tweaked), and some arrive as Tool-Provided globals from tools I install. When I start a new project I often copy skills by hand. That is messy: I forget where a skill lived, copies diverge across Managed Projects, and if I keep skills only as laptop globals, collaborators on a Project never get them. I want a single tool — **skillz** — that keeps Libraries as the union catalog of skills I (or my team/company) use, lets Managed Projects select and Lock Installations from those Libraries, and makes discovery, updates, Drift, and Promote straightforward — including a workplace flow where Library review can lag Project shipping.

## Solution

**skillz** is a CLI (with a future TUI) that replaces Skillfile in my workflow. It manages one or more Libraries (Personal, team, or company), registers Managed Projects (and a user-global `~/.agents/skills` scope) with ordered Library Bindings, and uses Locks so lasting Installations track Catalog Entries. Day-to-day editing and new-skill tryout happen **in the Project (or user) skills directory**; **`libcommit`** formalizes tested Installations into the Library workflow (new Catalog Entry, Library Branch Lock, or Overlay Fork). Discovery includes `skillz list --tag TAG`. git pre-commit and `jj push-with-checks` gate publishing Drift unless explicitly allowed. External Projects are observe/import only. Install scope is intentionally narrow — not Skillfile parity.

Agreed command-level usage is in `.scratch/skillz/usage-flows.md` and summarized under **Usage Flows** below.

## User Stories

1. As a solo developer, I want a Personal Library that is the union of skills I keep via libcommit from Managed use, so I always know what I standardize on.
2. As a solo developer, I want to record Authored Skills as Owned Entries, so my custom skills have a source of truth outside any one Project.
3. As a solo developer, I want Upstream Skills as Catalog Entries (source + Lock) without owning their content, so the Library stays a complete union without vendoring the internet.
4. As a solo developer, I want to Fork an Upstream or Tool-Provided skill into an Owned Entry when I edit it for keeps, so my tweaks are first-class Library content.
5. As a solo developer, I want Tool-Provided skills left out of the Library until I libcommit/promote them, so globals do not silently pollute the catalog.
6. As a library owner, I want to assign Tags to Catalog Entries, so I can discover skills by topic or toolchain.
7. As a library owner, I want `skillz list` (with filters such as `--tag TAG`), so I can find skills without remembering which Project last used them.
8. As a library owner, I want to search/list across bound Libraries for a Managed Project, so selection respects binding order and availability.
9. As a developer, I want to register a Project as Managed with an ordered list of Library Bindings, so skillz knows where Catalog Entries may come from.
10. As a developer, I want Library Bindings to be read-only or writable, so I can install from a company Library without being able to mutate it.
11. As a developer, I want to try a newly authored or fetched skill in my Project first, then `libcommit` it into a Library, so I test before the union catalog changes.
12. As a developer, I want skillz to materialize an Installation and record a Lock after add/libcommit, so the Project has pinned, reproducible skill content.
13. As a developer, I want Installations committed in the Project repo, so collaborators receive skills on clone without needing my Libraries.
14. As a collaborator, I want to clone a Managed Project and have skill files present, so agents work without running skillz first.
15. As a developer, I want to bump a Lock and reinstall when a Library entry advances, so Projects stay intentionally current.
16. As a developer, I want a Drift Report across Managed Projects, so I can see Installations that disagree with their Locks or with Library main line.
17. As a developer, I want Drift gates and reports to offer libcommit / Branch Lock / Overlay Fork / Promote as explicit next actions, so nothing silently merges into a Library.
18. As a developer, I want to Promote a skill change into a writable Library main line, so lasting shared edits land in the right source of truth.
19. As a developer in a workplace, I want `libcommit` to create a Library Branch Lock from my tested Installation, so I can ship the Project before main-line approval with an honest Lock.
20. As a developer in a workplace, I want a report of Managed Projects whose Locks are not on Library main line, so pre-merge usage is visible.
21. As a developer with a fully read-only Library, I want Overlay Fork into a writable bound Library via libcommit, so I can still ship Project-local skill changes honestly.
22. As a developer, I want External Projects (other people's clones) to be observable without forced Library membership, so skillz does not rewrite foreign repos.
23. As a developer, I want to explicitly import a skill from an External Project into a Library, so useful finds can join the union on purpose.
24. As a team lead, I want a shared team or company Library using the same skillz model, so the workplace uses one tool shape.
25. As a team member, I want my Managed Project to bind company → team → personal with precedence, so name conflicts resolve predictably.
26. As a Library maintainer, I want Promote / libcommit into a company Library to require an explicit writable target, so personal drift never silently writes company content.
27. As a developer starting a new Managed Project, I want to select skills already in Libraries via skillz list/add, so I stop hand-copying from old Projects.
28. As a developer, I want the Project skills directory to default to `.agents/skills` but be overridable (e.g. `.claude/skills`), so skillz fits my agent layout.
29. As a developer, I want to manage `~/.agents/skills` with the same skillz model (`skillz user …`), so user-global skills are not a separate ad-hoc mess.
30. As a developer migrating from Skillfile, I want import (including `-i` TUI adopt) into Catalog Entries + Locks, so I can leave Skillfile behind.
31. As a developer, I want a CLI named `skillz` as the primary interface, so I learn one tool.
32. As a developer, I want a future TUI over the same command API, so discovery, import adopt, and Drift review are pleasant.
33. As a developer, I want `skillz status` for a Managed Project or `--user`, so I can see Bindings, Installations, Locks, and Drift at a glance.
34. As a developer, I want `skillz list --tag` to accept repeated flags and comma-separated lists, so filtering matches how I think about Tags.
35. As a developer, I want list to show all Binding matches in precedence order by default, with optional `--dedupe`, so I can see overlays.
36. As a developer, I want list/add to show Availability across Project, user-global, and other agent skill roots (e.g. `.cursor/skills`, `.claude/skills`), so I know what the agent can already load.
37. As a developer, I want `add` to no-op/refresh when already in the Project and to warn when a skill exists only in user/other roots, so I do not assume collaborators see it.
38. As a developer, I want `skillz add --tag …` and `-i` multi-select, so I can pull many Library skills at once.
39. As a developer, I want `skillz fetch github:owner/repo SKILLNAME` to find nested skills, so Pocock-style layouts work.
40. As a developer, I want warnings (and `--with-deps`) when a skill references sibling skills (e.g. grill-with-docs → grilling, domain-modeling), so dependency graphs are less surprising.
41. As a developer, I want git pre-commit to block committing drifting skill files unless I allow Drift, so testing locally does not accidentally publish dishonest Locks.
42. As a developer on jj, I want `jj push-with-checks` (not `skillz push`) to drift-check before `jj git push`, so ordinary pushes stay normal and skill gates sit at the share boundary.
43. As a developer, I want `libcommit` as the verb that turns a tested Installation into Library + Lock state, so edit/add/new share one formalization step.
44. As an agent implementing skillz, I want one application command API as the test seam, so CLI and TUI share behavior.
45. As a Library owner, I want Libraries themselves to be ordinary versioned repos, so review/branch/PR workflows reuse existing source control.
46. As a developer, I want skillz to refuse to treat a Project as Managed until Bindings are configured, so External vs Managed stays explicit.
47. As a developer, I want to remove a skill from a Managed Project (Installation + Lock) without deleting it from the Library, so Projects can drop skills while the union catalog remains.
48. As a developer, I want to see which Managed Projects use a given Catalog Entry, so impact of a Library change is visible before I bump Locks.
49. As a developer, I want failed installs/libcommits to leave Project state consistent, so recovery is clear.
50. As a workplace admin, I want read-only Bindings to still allow install and list, so consumers are not blocked from discovery.

## Usage Flows

Canonical transcripts: `.scratch/skillz/usage-flows.md`.

### A — Library bootstrap
`library init` / `library add` / `library list`. Registry is **user-global** name → local path. Committed Project Bindings use shared **name + remote URL**. VCS inferred (`.jj/` → jj, else git).

### B — New Managed Project
`project init --bind …` writes Bindings + empty Locks; default `--skills-dir .agents/skills` (overridable). No skills installed yet. Hooks installed.

### B2 — User-global scope
`user init --bind …` manages `~/.agents/skills` with the same model; config/Locks in user skillz state.

### C — Convert existing Project
`project import --dry-run` / `--from skillfile` / `--adopt-local` / `-i` TUI per-skill upstream|authored|skip. Keep matching files; leftovers are Drift candidates. `user import` for home skills.

### D — Discovery
`list` with `--library` / `--user` / `--tag` (repeated and/or comma-separated, AND). Default: show all Binding hits in precedence order; `--dedupe` optional. Show **Availability**: Project `skills_dir`, user-global `~/.agents/skills`, and other known agent skill roots (e.g. `.agents/skills`, `.cursor/skills`, `.claude/skills`) even when they are not the install target.

### E — Add
- **E1** already in Library: `add` / `add --tag` / `-i` / `--with-deps`. Respect Availability: already in Project → no-op/refresh; only in user/other roots → warn that collaborators need a Project install.
- **E2/E3** new Upstream or Authored: **Project-first** via `fetch` / `new` into skills dir → test → **`libcommit --as upstream|authored`** into a writable Library (creates Catalog Entry + Lock). Until libcommit = Drift.

### F — Edit / libcommit / Promote
Edit Installation in place; `libcommit` → Branch Lock or Overlay Fork + update Lock; `promote` → Library main; `lock --main` after merge. git pre-commit blocks Drift; jj uses **`jj push-with-checks`**. Escape: `--allow-drift` / `SKILLZ_ALLOW_DRIFT=1`. No `skillz push` as jj entrypoint.

## Implementation Decisions

### Product name and interfaces
- Tool name: **skillz**. v1 CLI; TUI later on the same application command API.
- Replace Skillfile (ADR 0001); narrow install scope; no Skillfile parity.

### Domain rules
- Library = union catalog (Owned + Upstream references) for skills you libcommit/keep.
- Managed Project Bindings: ordered name+url+writability; local registry resolves path.
- Installations committed in Project skills dir (default `.agents/skills`).
- User-global scope: `~/.agents/skills`.
- Edit/new tryout in Installation; **libcommit** formalizes; **Promote** = main-line.
- Branch Lock primary; Overlay Fork fallback (ADR 0002).
- Drift never silent-synced.

### Discovery and deps
- Tags; list filters; no default dedupe.
- **Availability** column/flags on `list` / `add`: Project `skills_dir`, `~/.agents/skills`, plus known agent roots (`.agents/skills`, `.cursor/skills`, `.claude/skills`, …). Single install target remains `skills_dir`.
- Dep heuristics including Pocock `grill-with-docs` pattern; `--with-deps`.

### Metadata (ADR 0003)
- Project: `PROJECT/.skillz/skillz.toml` + `skillz.lock`; Installations in `skills_dir` (default `.agents/skills`).
- User registry: `~/.config/skillz/registry.toml` (Library name→path; Managed Project paths for Drift).
- User scope: `~/.config/skillz/user.toml` + `user.lock`; Installations in `~/.agents/skills`.
- Library repo: `library.toml` + Owned trees under e.g. `skills/`.
- Upstream `source`: `github:owner/repo[/path][@rev]` string in CLI and TOML (not structured fields).

### Architecture / test seam / stack (ADR 0004)
- Rust binary + `skillz-core` lib (application command API = test seam) with temp filesystem fixtures.
- `clap`; TOML via `toml`/`toml_edit`; shell out to `git`/`jj`.
- TUI later: `ratatui` + `crossterm`; not FrankenTUI for v1; thin UI boundary for a possible later swap.
- Libraries as normal git/jj repos; skillz lock format (not Skillfile.lock).

### Hooks
- git pre-commit on skill paths.
- jj: repo-local alias `jj push-with-checks` only (not `skillz push`).

## Testing Decisions

- Test external behavior of the application command API with fixture Libraries + Managed Projects (+ user-scope temp home).
- Cover: init/bind; import/-i; list tags & dedupe off/on; add from Library; fetch/new → libcommit; edit → libcommit Branch Lock; Overlay Fork; drift gates allow/deny; --with-deps warning path for grill-with-docs-like bodies; read-only library rejects libcommit target.
- CLI argv thin; TUI later. No prior art in-repo (greenfield).

## Out of Scope

- Skillfile coexistence layer; Skillfile-style long-lived patch pins as happy path.
- Silent cron sync into Libraries.
- Auto-Managing every clone under ~/code.
- Auto-import all Tool-Provided globals.
- Full multi-platform install matrix.
- Marketplace product; company auth beyond git hosting.
- TUI in the first vertical slice (API must allow it); FrankenTUI as v1 TUI backend.
- `skillz push` as the jj push command.
- Perfect dependency graphs from prose.

## Further Notes

- Glossary: `CONTEXT.md`.
- ADRs: `0001-replace-skillfile`, `0002-branch-lock-over-patches`, `0003-metadata-layout-and-source-strings`, `0004-rust-stack-ratatui-not-frankentui`.
- Usage/tech annex: `.scratch/skillz/usage-flows.md`.
- This repo uses jj + Beads (`br`, prefix `z`).
- Open polish: whether `libcommit` auto-chooses Overlay Fork vs requiring a flag; GitHub auth/`gh` vs raw git for private Upstream.
close_reason: All child implementation tickets closed (z-r9l.1–17); skillz vertical slice delivered

title: jj push-with-checks alias
description:
## Parent

z-r9l — Spec: skillz — skills manager CLI/TUI

## What to build

Repo-local jj alias `jj push-with-checks` that runs a cheap Drift check then `jj git push`. No `skillz push` entrypoint. No-op pass-through when skills are clean.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `hooks install` (or equivalent) can install the repo-local alias
- [ ] Drifting skills block push unless allow-drift escape is used
- [ ] Clean skills proceed to `jj git push`
- [ ] Ordinary `jj git push` remains available without skillz wrapping every push

title: library import: bulk Upstream from GitHub repo
description:
## What to build

`skillz library import <source> --library <name>` discovers every skill (`**/SKILL.md`) in a GitHub repo (or nested path) and upserts **Upstream Catalog Entries** into that Library only. No Project or `--user` Installations/Locks.

### CLI

```bash
skillz library import github:mattpocock/skills --library personal
skillz library import https://github.com/mattpocock/skills --library personal --dry-run
skillz library import github:mattpocock/skills --library personal --path skills/engineering
```

### Behavior

- Accept `github:owner/repo[/path][@rev]` **and** `https://github.com/owner/repo…` URLs; normalize to canonical `github:…@rev` in the catalog (ADR 0003).
- Clone/cache the repo (reuse existing fetch cache), walk for `SKILL.md`, skill name = containing directory name.
- Optional `--path <prefix>` limits discovery to that subtree (after optional source path).
- `--dry-run` lists what would be added/updated/skipped; writes nothing.
- Apply: upsert Upstream entries; identical source+name → no-op/skip; name collision with different source → report and skip (or error clearly — prefer skip+warn for bulk).
- Does **not** materialize into any Managed Project or user-global skills dir.
- Works against a registered Library by name (writable); does not require cwd to be a Managed Project.

### Acceptance

- [ ] `library import --help` documents source forms, `--library`, `--dry-run`, `--path`
- [ ] HTTPS and `github:` sources both work; catalog stores `github:…@rev` with per-skill path
- [ ] Importing `mattpocock/skills` (or a fixture tree) creates Upstream entries for each discovered skill
- [ ] `--dry-run` prints the plan and leaves `library.toml` unchanged
- [ ] `--path skills/engineering` imports only under that prefix
- [ ] No files appear under a Project/`--user` skills dir as a side effect
- [ ] Tests cover discovery, URL normalize, dry-run, path filter, collision skip
close_reason: Met AC: library import discovers github/https sources, dry-run/path/collision, catalog-only upsert + tests

title: library import -i multi-select
description:
## What to build

Interactive multi-select on top of `skillz library import` discovery so the user can choose a subset of skills before upserting Upstream Catalog Entries.

### CLI

```bash
skillz library import github:mattpocock/skills --library personal -i
skillz library import github:mattpocock/skills --library personal --path skills/engineering -i
```

### Behavior

- Reuse the same discovery + URL normalize + catalog-only upsert as non-interactive import.
- `-i` / `--interactive` presents a TUI (or Prompter) multi-select of discovered skills (name + relative path); confirm applies only the selected set.
- Combines with `--path` (filter discovery first) and refuses `--dry-run -i` or treats dry-run as preview-only without apply (document one behavior: prefer erroring on `--dry-run -i`).
- Still never materializes Installations.

### Acceptance

- [ ] `library import -i` lets user select a subset and only those become Upstream entries
- [ ] Cancel/quit leaves the Library unchanged
- [ ] Works with `--path`
- [ ] Help documents `-i`
- [ ] Smoke/test or TUI harness covers select→apply

**Blocked by:** library import: bulk Upstream from GitHub repo
close_reason: Met AC: -i multi-select subset/cancel/path; dry-run -i errors; Prompter harness + help

title: drift remove: warn when skill is a dependency of a retained skill
description:
## What to build

When removing a skill via `skillz drift` (interactive Remove action), warn if any **retained** Installation appears to depend on the skill being removed (best-effort reverse of existing sibling-dep heuristics). Soft warn + confirm — do not hard-block.

### Behavior

- When queueing or confirming Remove in `drift -i`, scan other skills that will remain (not also queued for Remove) with `deps::detect_sibling_deps` (or a reverse helper) and list dependants.
- Surface in the existing confirm-remove modal (e.g. `grilling` is referenced by: grill-with-docs).
- User can still confirm Remove; Library catalog is untouched (existing remove semantics).
- Non-interactive path: if/when remove is exposed outside TUI, print the same warning to stderr before proceeding.

### Acceptance

- [ ] Removing a dep of a retained skill shows a warn listing dependant skill names in the confirm UI
- [ ] Removing a skill with no reverse deps keeps the existing confirm flow
- [ ] Bulk remove of both dependant and dependency does not warn about the pair being removed together
- [ ] Warn is soft (y still removes); Library unchanged
- [ ] Unit test for reverse-dep detection helper

**Blocked by:** None — can start immediately
close_reason: Met AC: reverse-dep helper + confirm UI warn; soft; bulk pair quiet; Library untouched

title: Agent skill for managing skills with skillz (+ tool-provided install provenance)
description:
## Summary

Ship a skillz-authored skill that teaches agents how to use the `skillz` CLI to manage Libraries, Catalog Entries, Installations, Locks, Drift, and related workflows — and implement Tool-Provided cataloging per ADR 0005 so skillz can re-install from the providing tool instead of a Library mirror.

## Design

Resolved in grill (see Design field + ADR 0005 + CONTEXT.md). Tool-Provided → explicit libcommit → Upstream `cmd:` template reference; eager validate install + version probe at catalog time; Locks pin observational tool version; Project add always runs the template.

## Deliverables

1. `cmd:` / `|version:` Upstream source support + validation + materialize (ADR 0005)
2. Agent-facing skill documenting skillz workflows (including Tool-Provided cataloging once available)
design:
## Resolved (grill 2026-11-10)

Tool-Provided enters Library only on explicit libcommit as an Upstream reference (not Owned), unless later Forked.
No third EntryKind: extend Upstream source strings (ADR 0005).
Catalog source = command template, e.g. `cmd:rexpad skill install --dir {dir}`; skillz substitutes `{dir}` (never host paths in the string).
Optional `|version:…` override; default version probe is `{argv0} --version`.
`@rev` optional in catalog; required on Locks as observational tool version (ordering/newer), not content hash.
Eager validation at Library add/libcommit: confirm install template + version probe succeed (parallel to checking github when cataloging). Do not defer syntax/tool failures to Project add.
Project materialize/refresh always invokes the template; no Library mirror fallback; missing tool → clear error. Collaborators still use committed Project Installations.

See ADR 0005 and CONTEXT.md (Tool-Provided Skill, Upstream Skill).
acceptance_criteria:
Upstream cmd: source grammar with {dir} (and documented placeholders) plus optional |version:…
libcommit/catalog of Tool-Provided validates install + version probe before recording the Catalog Entry
Locks store observational tool version (@rev); catalogs may omit it
Project/user add from such an entry runs the template; missing tool fails clearly; no Library file mirror
CONTEXT.md + ADR 0005 remain accurate
Agent-facing skill documents how to manage skills with skillz (including Tool-Provided / cmd: cataloging when implemented)
notes: Design question resolved via grill-with-docs. Implementation should follow ADR 0005. Remaining work: cmd:/version grammar + validation + materialize path; plus the agent-facing skillz-management skill (may split).
close_reason: Met AC: cmd: Upstream sources + eager validation/materialize (ADR 0005); skillz agent skill authored
